title: When KV Cache Beats GPU Compute

beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how When KV Cache Beats GPU Compute cuts 98.5% of memory overhead.
beats.visual_focus: System architecture schematic illustrating When KV Cache Beats GPU  highlighted in pulsing cyan.

beats.text: The core challenge? We study such a tier in a disaggregated deployment of GLM-5.3. An FP8 mixture-of-experts model with multi-head latent attention (MLA). On 8xB300 nodes running prefill context parallelism (PCP8).
beats.visual_focus: Bottleneck diagram showing resource contention and latency backup.

beats.text: Enter When KV Cache Beats GPU. Enabling the remote tier (LMCache with a Valkey store) left median time-to-first-token unchanged but raised the 16k-token p99 from 3.96 s to 17.3 s.
beats.visual_focus: Parallel pipeline splitting heavy operations away from the critical execution path.

beats.text: Under the hood. Replaying a production request stream on an isolated engine. We find that a remote hit took 0.88 s against 0.31 s to recompute the prompt. That synchronous loading turned a hit-heavy stream into an unstable queue. P99 83.32 s with the GPUs 7% busy.

beats.text: The result? A two-term cost model explains both. A hit pays off only if the tier delivers more than B* = sR (2.53 GB/s for this model and GPU). And a fixed per-hit engine cost (T0 ~ 0.33 s) means that hits on prompts shorter than about 17k tokens cannot beat recompute at any bandwidth.
